subject: Procurement & packaging options for Redwood - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@finco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement & packaging options for Redwood - next steps

Thanks again for the call today — great to connect. Quick recap and suggested next steps so procurement has what you need to move forward:

Recap: we covered production use (low-latency customer-facing features), expected monthly token volume (~50M tokens/month initially), and data residency / SOC 2 requirements. FinCo indicated preference for PO-based billing and marketplace procurement is an option to evaluate.

Recommended commercial paths (high level):
- Hosted (Redwood API, pay-as-you-go/credit card): fastest onboarding, no commit; good for proofs-of-concept or low-volume pilots.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity): recommended if you need predictable throughput; typically requires a committed monthly/annual spend (commits), invoiced via PO/Net30 for enterprise customers.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): for regulated environments; enterprise contract + platform fees; procurement and security reviews required.

Procurement items I can provide today: pricing workbook with lines for hosted vs dedicated vs private, a one-page procurement checklist, our sample PO template, and SOC 2 attestation. I've attached: Redwood-Procurement-Checklist.pdf, Redwood-Pricing-Options-2026.xlsx, PO-template-FinCo.docx.

Questions for you to confirm:
1) Do you prefer AWS Marketplace or direct vendor invoice (PO + Net30)?
2) Who should be the procurement contact (name + email) to receive the PO and insurance/COI?
3) Any additional legal or compliance docs required upfront (DPA/Addendum)?

Next steps: if you confirm PO + Net30 + marketplace interest, I can loop in our finance and legal to speed the paperwork. If you prefer to start on hosted with card to expedite a pilot, we can enable that this week.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min procurement-only call if that helps.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachments: Redwood-Procurement-Checklist.pdf (application/pdf, 120KB); Redwood-Pricing-Options-2026.xlsx (spreadsheet); PO-template-FinCo.docx (document)
From: Jillian Park <j.park@finco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:34:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Procurement & packaging options for Redwood - next steps

Thanks Marissa — useful summary. A few clarifying questions from procurement: 

1) We prefer PO + Net30 for anything invoiced to Finance. Is Redwood able to accept a PO and invoice on Net30 terms for Dedicated?
2) We would also prefer buying via AWS Marketplace if possible (reduces procurement friction). Is your offering listed there and do you have marketplace pricing that maps to the committed/usage models?
3) For Private deployments, we need confirmation on SLAs and data residency (we host in east/us). Do you have a standard SLA doc?

Also — do you require a signature on the SOW or is a PO enough to start provisioning? If you can share an example SOW and the PO template we can circulate internally.

Procurement contact: Jillian Park, j.park@finco.com

Thanks — once we have these answers I'll route to Finance for approval.

Best,
Jillian
Senior Procurement Manager, FinCo
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jillian Park <j.park@finco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement & packaging options for Redwood - next steps

Jillian — thanks, answers inline below and attaching the sample SOW + pricing breakout.

1) PO + Net30: yes — we can accept a PO + Net30 invoice for Dedicated and Private engagements. For Hosted (pay-as-you-go) customers we often enable card billing; however, enterprise customers can also be set up on invoiced terms if we have an executed order form and credit terms.

2) AWS Marketplace: we are listed on AWS Marketplace. Marketplace SKUs typically map to hosted on-demand pricing; we can also support marketplace contracts that cover committed Dedicated purchases in select cases (marketplace consolidation and billing needs a bit more coordination). If marketplace is preferred, we will engage our partnerships team to confirm mapping for the committed model.

3) SLA & data residency: we have a standard SLA for Dedicated/Private with uptime targets and response windows; I attached the SLA excerpt and SOC 2 summary. For data residency, we support region-specific deployments (we can provision in us-east).

4) Signature vs PO: a PO plus our signed order form / executed SOW is our typical legal trigger for provisioning Dedicated capacity. For smaller hosted pilots, we can start on card or with a short-term trial credit without a PO.

Attached: Redwood-Pricing-Options-2026.xlsx (pricing lines for hosted/dedicated/private), SOW-sample-Redwood-v1.docx, SLA-excerpt.pdf.

Suggested next step: would you be open to a 30-minute procurement call this week to confirm whether to go marketplace (fast for AWS customers) or direct PO/Net30? If marketplace is preferred, I'll loop in our partnerships lead.

If helpful, proposed commercial path we recommend for FinCo given your volume: start hosted for rapid validation (card or short PO) -> 90-day pilot on Dedicated with a small commit (convert to full commit post pilot) -> Private if regulatory controls require it. This keeps procurement friction low while allowing capacity and cost predictability once you scale.

—
Marissa
Attachments: SOW-sample-Redwood-v1.docx; SLA-excerpt.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Procurement & packaging options for Redwood - next steps

FYI forwarding the procurement thread with FinCo. Key notes: they prefer PO + Net30 and would like marketplace if possible. Procurement contact is Jillian Park (j.park@finco.com).

My suggested commercial play: propose a hybrid path — start hosted to validate prod integration (card or short invoiced pilot), then move to a 90-day Dedicated pilot with a small commit invoiced via PO/Net30. If procurement will only approve marketplace purchases, we need to confirm whether we can map the Dedicated commit to a marketplace SKU or else get an exception.

Questions for you:
- Aditya: can partnerships confirm Dedicated commit -> marketplace mapping and whether finance can accept marketplace for committed SKUs?
- Laura: can you confirm whether we can offer 90-day pilot credits/contracting flexibility for this account?

I'll wait to hear back before scheduling procurement call.

Thanks,
Marissa
